summary: Scanned the full git history (5 commits) and the working tree of leaky-repo with gitleaks 8.30.1. Two real credentials leaked: an AWS access key pair that is removed from HEAD but still in history, and a GitHub token in scripts/release.sh. One hit is a random key planted as a test fixture, dismissed as a false positive.

findings.title: AWS access key pair committed in .env (still in git history)
findings.description: An AWS access key ID (AKIA************) and its secret key were committed in .env by commit 1716f94 and deleted in the next commit. The pair is still readable in history by anyone with a clone.

proof.poc: gitleaks git --redact --report-format json --report-path gitleaks.json . && jq '.[] | select(.RuleID=="aws-access-token") | {File, StartLine, Commit}' gitleaks.json

findings.remediation: Deactivate and rotate the key pair in IAM now, review CloudTrail for its use, then purge .env from history and add a gitleaks pre-commit hook.

findings.title: GitHub personal access token hardcoded in scripts/release.sh
findings.description: A GitHub personal access token (ghp_************) is passed in an Authorization header in scripts/release.sh and is present in HEAD.

proof.poc: gitleaks git --redact --report-format json --report-path gitleaks.json . && jq '.[] | select(.RuleID=="github-pat") | {File, StartLine, Commit}' gitleaks.json

findings.remediation: Revoke the token in GitHub settings, read it from the environment or a secret store, and add a gitleaks pre-commit hook.

hypotheses.title: generic-api-key hit in tests/test_client.py
hypotheses.rationale: gitleaks reports a generic-api-key on a random value planted in tests/test_client.py; the file marks it as a dummy credential for the mocked transport. It is not a real credential.
hypotheses.next_step: None. Dismissed as a test fixture.
